Under the assumptions of Prop. E.1, we have

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}^{w^{\textup{i.i.d.{}}}}_{n},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]\geq\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]\geq\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}^{w^{\textup{sr}}}_{n},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]. $$

#### Proof of Prop. E.2.

Let $K\triangleq{\bm{k}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ . To show the first inequality, note that since $\eta=\frac{mw-\lfloor mw\rfloor}{r}$ , by Prop. E.1,

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})] \textstyle=\frac{r(\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R,R)-\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R,R^{\prime}))}{m^{2}} \textstyle=\frac{r(\sum_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\eta_{i}-\sum_{i,j\in[n]}K_{ij}\eta_{i}\eta_{j})}{m^{2}} \textstyle=\frac{1}{m}\left(\sum_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\left(w_{i}-\frac{\lfloor mw_{i}\rfloor}{m}\right)-\frac{m}{r}\left(w-\frac{\lfloor mw\rfloor}{m}\right)^{\top}K\left(w-\frac{\lfloor mw\rfloor}{m}\right)\right). $$

Hence

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{i.i.d.{}}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]-\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})] \textstyle= \textstyle\frac{1}{m}\left(\sum_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\frac{\lfloor mw_{i}\rfloor}{m}+\frac{m}{r}\left(w-\frac{\lfloor mw\rfloor}{m}\right)^{\top}K\left(w-\frac{\lfloor mw\rfloor}{m}\right)-w^{\top}Kw\right) \textstyle= \textstyle\frac{1}{m}\left((1-\theta)\sum_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\xi_{i}+\theta\eta^{\top}K\eta-w^{\top}Kw\right), $$

where we let $\xi\triangleq\frac{m}{m-r}\frac{\lfloor mw\rfloor}{m}$ and $\theta\triangleq\frac{r}{m}$ . Note that $w=\theta\eta+(1-\theta)\xi$ . By Lem. E.1 and Jensen’s inequality, we have

$$ \textstyle w^{\top}Kw \textstyle=E_{\bm{k}}(w)\leq\theta E_{\bm{k}}(\eta)+(1-\theta)E_{\bm{k}}(\xi)=\theta\eta^{\top}K\eta+(1-\theta)\xi^{\top}K\xi\leq\theta\eta^{\top}K\eta+(1-\theta)\sum_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\xi_{i}, $$

where the last inequality follows from Prop. E.1(a) with $w=\xi$ and the fact that MMD is nonnegative. Hence we have shown

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{i.i.d.{}}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]-\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]\geq 0, $$

as desired.

For the second inequality, by Prop. E.1, we compute

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]-\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{sr}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]=\frac{r}{m^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{r}\sum_{j\in[r]}\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R_{j},R^{\prime}_{j})-\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R,R^{\prime})\right). $$

Note that

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R,R^{\prime})=\int_{[0,1)}\int_{[0,1)}k(x_{D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}}(u)},x_{D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}}(v)})\differential u\differential v=E_{\bm{k}}\left((D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}})_{\#}\textup{Uniform}[0,1)\right), $$

where we used $T_{\#}\mu$ to denote the pushforward measure of $\mu$ by $T$ . Similarly,

$$ \textstyle\frac{1}{r}\sum_{j\in[r]}\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R_{j},R^{\prime}_{j}) \textstyle=\frac{1}{r}\sum_{j\in[r]}\int_{[\frac{j}{r},\frac{j+1}{r})}\int_{[\frac{j}{r},\frac{j+1}{r})}k(x_{D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}}(u)},x_{D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}}(v)})\differential u\differential v \textstyle=\frac{1}{r}\sum_{j\in[r]}E_{\bm{k}}\left((D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}})_{\#}\textup{Uniform}\left[\frac{j}{r},\frac{j+1}{r}\right)\right) \textstyle\leq E_{\bm{k}}\left((D_{\eta}^{\textup{inv}})_{\#}\textup{Uniform}[0,1)\right)=\mathbb{E}{\bm{k}}(R,R^{\prime}), $$

where in the last inequality we applied Jensen’s inequality since $E_{\bm{k}}$ is convex by Lem. E.1. Hence we have shown

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{resid}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]-\mathbb{E}[\mmd^{2}_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{sr}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w})]\geq 0 $$

and the proof is complete. ∎

## Appendix F Accelerated Debiased Compression

In this section, we provide supplementary algorithmic details and deferred analyses for LSKT (Alg. 3). In WeightedRPCholesky (Alg. F.1), we provide details for the weighted extension of Chen et al. [2022, Alg. 2.1] that is used extensively in our algorithms. The details of AMD [Wang et al., 2023, Alg. 14] are provided in Alg. F.2. In Sec. F.1, we give the proof of Thm. 4 for the MMD error guarantee of LD (Alg. 2). In Sec. F.2, we provide details on KT-Compress++ modified from Compress++ [Shetty et al., 2022] to minimize MMD to $\mathbb{P}$ . Finally, Thm. 5 is proved in Sec. F.3.

*Algorithm F.1 Weighted Randomly Pivoted Cholesky (WeightedRPCholesky) (extension of Chen et al. [2022, Alg. 2.1])*

```
Input: kernel ${\bm{k}}$ , points $\mathcal{S}_{n}=(x_{i})_{i=1}^{n}$ , simplex weights $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , rank $r$
$\tilde{\bm{k}}(i,j)\triangleq{\bm{k}}(x_{i},x_{j})\sqrt{w_{i}}\sqrt{w_{j}}$ $\triangleright$ reweighted kernel matrix function
$F\leftarrow\bm{0}_{n\times r},\mathtt{S}\leftarrow\{\},d\leftarrow(\tilde{\bm{k}}(i,i))_{i\in[n]}$
for $i=1$ to $r$ do
Sample $s\sim d/\sum_{j\in[n]}d_{j}$
$\mathtt{S}\leftarrow\mathtt{S}\cup\{s\}$
$g\leftarrow\tilde{\bm{k}}(:,s)-F(:,1:i-1)F(s,1:i-1)^{\top}$
$F(:,i)\leftarrow g/\sqrt{g_{s}}$
$d\leftarrow d-F(:,i)^{2}$ $\triangleright$ $F(:,i)^{2}$ denotes a vector with entry-wise squared values of $F(:,i)$
$d\leftarrow\max(d,0)$ $\triangleright$ numerical stability fix, helpful in practice
end for
$F\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}((1/\sqrt{w_{i}})_{i\in[n]})F$ $\triangleright$ undo weighting; treat $1/\sqrt{w_{i}}=0$ if $w_{i}=0$
Return: $\mathtt{S}\subset[n]$ with $\absolutevalue{\tS}=r$ and $F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}$
```

*Algorithm F.2 Accelerated Entropic Mirror Descent (AMD) (modification of Wang et al. [2023, Alg. 14])*

```
Input: kernel matrix $K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ , number of steps $T$ , initial weight $w_{0}\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , aggressive flag AGG
$\eta\leftarrow\frac{1}{8w_{0}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(K)}$ if AGG else $\frac{1}{8\max_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}}$
$v_{0}\leftarrow w_{0}$
for $t=1$ to $T$ do
$\beta_{t}\leftarrow\frac{2}{t+1}$
$z_{t}\leftarrow(1-\beta_{t})w_{t-1}+\beta_{t}v_{t-1}$
$g\leftarrow 2t\eta Kz_{t}$ $\triangleright$ this is $\gamma_{t}\nabla f(z_{t})$ in Wang et al. [2023, Alg. 14] for $f(w)=w^{\top}Kw$
$v_{t}\leftarrow v_{t-1}\cdot\exp(-g)$ $\triangleright$ component-wise exponentiation and multiplication
$v_{t}\leftarrow v_{t}/\left\|{v_{t}}\right\|_{1}$ $\triangleright$ $v_{t}=\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w\in\Delta_{n-1}}\langle g,w\rangle+D_{v_{t-1}}^{\phi}(w)$ for $\phi(w)=\sum_{i\in[n]}w_{i}\log w_{i}$
$w_{t}\leftarrow(1-\beta_{t})w_{t-1}+\beta_{t}v_{t}$
end for
Return: $w_{T}\in\Delta_{n-1}$
```

### F.1 Proof of Thm. 4: Theorem 4 (Debiasing guarantee for LD).

We start with a useful lemma that bounds $w^{\top}(K-\hat{K})w$ by $\tr(K-\hat K)$ for any simplex weights $w$ .

#### Lemma F.1.

For any PSD matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , we have

$$ \textstyle w^{\top}Aw\leq\tr(A^w)\leq\max_{i\in[n]}A_{ii}\leq\lambda_{1}(A), $$

where $\lambda_{1}(A)$ denotes the largest eigenvalue of $A$ .

#### Proof of Lem. F.1.

Note that

$$ \textstyle w^{\top}Aw \textstyle=\sqrt{w}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w})A\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w})\sqrt{w}=\sqrt{w}^{\top}A^{w}\sqrt{w}. $$

The condition that $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ implies $\left\|{\sqrt{w}}\right\|_{2}=1$ , so that

$$ \textstyle\sqrt{w}^{\top}A^{w}\sqrt{w}\leq\lambda_{1}(A^{w})\leq\tr(A^w). $$

To see $\tr(A^w)\leq\max{i\in[n]}A_{ii}$ , note that $\tr(A^w)=\sum_{i\in[n]}A_{ii}w_{i}\leq\max_{i\in[n]}A_{ii}$ since $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ ..

Since $\lambda_{1}(A)=\sup_{x:\left\|{x}\right\|_{2}=1}x^{\top}Ax$ , if we let $i^{*}\triangleq\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{i\in[n]}A_{ii}$ , then the simplex weight with $1$ on the $i^{*}$ -th entry has two-norm $1$ , so we see that $\max_{i\in[n]}A_{ii}\leq\lambda_{1}(A)$ . ∎

Our next lemma bounds the suboptimality of surrogate optimization of a low-rank plus diagonal approximation of $K$ .

#### Lemma F.2 (Suboptimality of surrogate optimization).

Let ${{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ be a kernel satisfying Assum. 1. Let $\mathcal{S}_{n}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a sequence of points. Define $K\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ . Suppose $\widehat{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is another PSD matrix such that $K\succeq\widehat{K}$ . Define $D\triangleq\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K})$ , the diagonal part of $K-\widehat{K}$ , and form $K^{\prime}\triangleq\widehat{K}+D$ . Let $w^{\prime}\in\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w\in\Delta_{n-1}}w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime}$ . Then for any $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{P})\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\tr((K - \widehat K)^w)+\max_{i\in[n]}(K-\widehat{K})_{ii}+(w^{\top}K^{\prime}w-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime}). $$

#### Proof of Lem. F.2.

Since $K=K^{\prime}+(K-\widehat{K})-D$ by construction, we have

$$ \textstyle w^{\top}Kw \textstyle=w^{\top}K^{\prime}w+w^{\top}(K-\widehat{K})w-w^{\top}Dw \textstyle\leq w^{\top}K^{\prime}w+w^{\top}(K-\widehat{K})w \textstyle=(w^{\top}K^{\prime}w-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime})+w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime}+w^{\top}(K-\widehat{K})w \textstyle\leq(w^{\top}K^{\prime}w-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime})+w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime}+\tr((K-\widehat K)^w), $$

where we used the fact that $D\succeq 0$ and Lem. F.1. Next, by the definition of $w^{\prime}$ , we have

$$ \textstyle w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime} \textstyle\leq({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}K^{\prime}{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}=({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}(K^{\prime}-K){w_{\textsc{OPT}}}+({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}K{w_{\textsc{OPT}}} \textstyle=({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}(D-(K-\widehat{K})){w_{\textsc{OPT}}}+({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}K{w_{\textsc{OPT}}} \textstyle\leq({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}D{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}+({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}K{w_{\textsc{OPT}}} \textstyle\leq\max_{i\in[n]}(K-\widehat{K})_{ii}+({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})^{\top}K{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}, $$

where we used the fact $K\succeq\widehat{K}$ in the penultimate step and Lem. F.1 in the last step. Hence we have shown our claim. ∎

Lem. F.2 shows that to control $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{P})$ , it suffices to separately control the approximation error in terms of $\tr(K - \hat K)$ and the optimization error $(w^{\top}K^{\prime}w-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime})$ . The next result establishes that using WeightedRPCholesky, we can obtain polynomial and exponential decay bounds for $\tr(K-\hat K)$ in expectation depending on the kernel growth of ${{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ .

#### Proposition F.1 (Approximation error of WeightedRPCholesky).

Let ${\bm{k}}$ be a kernel satisfying Assum. ( α , β )-kernel. Let $\mathcal{S}_{\infty}$ be an infinite sequence of points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . For any $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , let $F$ be the low-rank approximation factor output by $\hyperref@@ii[alg:rpc]{\textup{WeightedRPCholesky}}({\bm{k}},\mathcal{S}_{n},w,r)$ . Define $K\triangleq{\bm{k}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ . If $r\geq(\frac{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}+1}{\sqrt{\log 2}}+\sqrt{\log 2})^{2}-\frac{1}{\log 2}$ , then, with the expectation taken over the randomness in WeightedRPCholesky,

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\tr\left((K-FF^{\top})^{w}\right)\right]\leq H_{n,r}, $$

where $H_{n,r}$ is defined as

$$ \textstyle H_{n,r}\triangleq\begin{cases}8\sum_{\ell=\mathfrak{U}(r)}^{n}(\frac{L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})}{\ell})^{\frac{2}{\alpha}}&\hyperref@@ii[assum:kernel_growth]{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\textsc{PolyGrowth}}}({\alpha},{\beta}),\\
8\sum_{\ell=\mathfrak{U}(r)}^{n}\exp(1-(\frac{\ell}{\krcd_\k(R_n)})^{\frac{1}{\alpha}})&\hyperref@@ii[assum:kernel_growth]{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\textsc{LogGrowth}}}({\alpha},{\beta}),\end{cases} $$

for $L_{\bm{k}}$ defined in (32) and

$$ \textstyle\mathfrak{U}(r)\triangleq\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{r+\frac{1}{\log 2}}{\log 2}}-\frac{1}{\log 2}\right\rfloor. $$

Moreover, $H_{n,r}$ satisfies the bounds in Thm. 4.

#### Proof of Prop. F.1.

Recall the notation $L_{{\bm{k}}}(R_{n})=\frac{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}}{\log 2}$ from (32). Define $q\triangleq\mathfrak{U}(r)$ so that $q$ is the biggest integer for which $r\geq 2q+q^{2}\log 2$ . The lower bound assumption of $r$ is chosen such that $q>L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})>0$ . By Chen et al. [2022, Theorem 3.1] with $\epsilon=1$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\tr\left((K-FF^{\top})^{w}\right)\right]\leq 2\sum_{\ell=q+1}^{n}\lambda_{\ell}(K^{w}). $$

Since $q>L_{k}(R_{n})$ , we can apply Cor. B.1 to bound $\lambda_{\ell}(K^{w})$ for $\ell\geq q+1$ and obtain (289) since $H_{n,r}$ (290) is constructed to match the bounds when applying Cor. B.1 to (292). It remains to justify the bounds for $H_{n,r}$ in Thm. 4.

If ${\bm{k}}$ is $\hyperref@@ii[assum:kernel_growth]{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\textsc{PolyGrowth}}}({\alpha},{\beta})$ , by Assum. ( α , β )-kernel we have ${\alpha}<2$ . Hence

$$ \textstyle H_{n,r} \textstyle=8\sum_{\ell=q}^{n}\left(\frac{L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})}{\ell}\right)^{\frac{2}{{\alpha}}}\leq 8L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})^{\frac{2}{{\alpha}}}\int_{q-1}^{\infty}\ell^{-\frac{2}{{\alpha}}}\differential\ell=8L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})^{\frac{2}{{\alpha}}}(q-1)^{1-\frac{2}{{\alpha}}}=O\left(\sqrt{r}(\frac{R_{n}^{2\beta}}{r})^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}\right), $$

where we used the fact that $\int_{q-1}^{\infty}\ell^{-\frac{2}{\alpha}}\differential\ell=(q-1)^{1-\frac{2}{\alpha}}$ for $\alpha<2$ , $L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})=O(R_{n}^{\beta})$ , and $q=\Theta(\sqrt{r})$ .

If ${\bm{k}}$ is $\hyperref@@ii[assum:kernel_growth]{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\textsc{LogGrowth}}}({\alpha},{\beta})$ , then

$$ \textstyle H_{n,r} \textstyle=8\sum_{\ell=q}^{n}\exp(1-\left(\frac{\ell}{\krcd_\k(R_n)}\right)^{\frac{1}{\cvrw}})=8e\sum_{\ell=q}^{n}c^{\ell^{1/\alpha}}\leq 8e\int_{\ell=q-1}^{\infty}c^{\ell^{1/\alpha}}, $$

where $c\triangleq\exp(-\krcd_\k(R_n)^{-1/\alpha})\in(0,1)$ . Defining $m\triangleq-\log c>0$ and $q^{\prime}=q-1$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\int_{x=q^{\prime}}^{\infty}c^{x^{1/\alpha}}\differential x=\int_{x=q^{\prime}}^{\infty}\exp(-mx^{1/\alpha})\differential x \textstyle=\alpha q^{\prime}(mq^{\prime 1/\alpha})^{-\alpha}\Gamma(\alpha,mq^{\prime 1/\alpha})=\alpha m^{-\alpha}\Gamma(\alpha,mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}), $$

where $\Gamma(\alpha,x)\triangleq\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{\alpha-1}e^{-t}\differential t$ is the incomplete gamma function. Since $\alpha>0$ , by Pinelis [2020, Thm. 1.1], we have

$$ \textstyle\Gamma(\alpha,mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}) \textstyle\leq\frac{(mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}+b)^{\alpha}-(mq^{\prime 1/\alpha})^{\alpha}}{\alpha b}e^{-mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}}, $$

where $b$ is a known constant depending only on $\alpha$ . By the equivalence of norms on $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ , there exists $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that $(x+y)^{\alpha}\leq C_{\alpha}(x^{\alpha}+y^{\alpha})$ for any $x,y>0$ . Hence

$$ \textstyle\Gamma(\alpha,mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}) \textstyle\leq\frac{(mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}+b)^{\alpha}}{\alpha b}e^{-mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}}\leq\frac{C_{\alpha}(m^{\alpha}q^{\prime}+b^{\alpha})}{\alpha b}e^{-mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}}. $$

Hence from (295) we deduce

$$ \textstyle\sum_{\ell=q^{\prime}}^{\infty}c^{\ell^{1/\alpha}} \textstyle\leq C_{\alpha}(q^{\prime}b^{-1}+b^{\alpha-1}m^{-\alpha})e^{-mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}}. $$

Since $m=-\log c=L_{\bm{k}}(R_{n})^{-1/\alpha}$ , we can bound the exponent by

$$ \textstyle-mq^{\prime 1/\alpha}=-(L_{k}(R_{n})^{-1}q^{\prime})^{1/\alpha}=-(\frac{q^{\prime}\log 2}{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}})^{1/\alpha}\leq-(\frac{0.83\sqrt{r}-2.39}{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}})^{1/\alpha}, $$

where we used the fact that $q^{\prime}\log 2=(q-1)\log 2\geq(\sqrt{\frac{r+\frac{1}{\log 2}}{\log 2}}-\frac{1}{\log 2}-2)\log 2\geq 0.83\sqrt{r}-2.39$ . On the other hand, since $q^{\prime}=q-1\geq L(R_{n})=m^{-\alpha}$ , we can absorb the $b^{\alpha-1}m^{-1}$ term in (298) into $q$ and finally obtain the bounds for $H_{n,r}$ in Thm. 4. ∎

The last piece of our analysis involves bounding the optimization error $(w^{\top}K^{\prime}w-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime})$ in (280).

#### Lemma F.3 (AMD guarantee for debiasing).

Let $K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be an SPSD matrix. Let $f(w)\triangleq w^{\top}Kw$ . Then the final iterate $x_{T}$ of Nesterov’s 1-memory method [Wang et al., 2023, Algorithm 14] after $T$ steps with objective function $f(w)$ , norm $\left\|{\cdot}\right\|=\left\|{\cdot}\right\|_{1}$ , distance-generating function $\phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_{i}\log x_{i}$ , and initial point $w_{0}=(\frac{1}{n},\ldots,\frac{1}{n})\in\Delta_{n-1}$ satisfies

$$ \textstyle f(w_{T})-f({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})\leq\frac{16\log n\max_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}}{T^{2}}, $$

where ${w_{\textsc{OPT}}}\in\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}}f(x)$ .

#### Proof of Lem. F.3.

We apply Wang et al. [2023, Theorem 14]. Hence it remains to determine the smoothness constant $L>0$ such that, for all $x,y\in\Delta_{n-1}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\left\|{\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)}\right\|_{\infty}\leq L\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{1}, $$

and an upper bound for the Bregman divergence $D^{\phi}_{w_{0}}({w_{\textsc{OPT}}})=\sum_{i=1}^{n}{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}_{i}\log\frac{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}_{i}}{(w_{0})_{i}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}_{i}\log n{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}_{i}$ . To determine $L$ , note $\nabla f(w)=2Kw$ , so we have, for any $x,y\in\Delta_{n-1}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\left\|{\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)}\right\|_{\infty} \textstyle=2\left\|{K(x-y)}\right\|_{\infty}=2\max_{i\in[n]}\absolutevalue{K_{i, :} (x-y)} \textstyle\leq 2\max_{i\in[n]}\left\|{K_{i,:}}\right\|_{\infty}\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{1}=2\left(\max_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\right)\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{1}=2\left(\max_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}\right)\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{1}, $$

where we used the fact that the largest entry in an SPSD matrix appears on its diagonal. Thus we can take the smoothness constant to be

$$ \textstyle L=2\max_{i\in[n]}K_{ii}. $$

To bound $D^{\phi}_{w_{0}}({{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}})$ , note that by Jensen’s inequality,

$$ \textstyle D^{\phi}_{w_{0}}({w})=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\log nw_{i}\leq\log(\sum_{i=1}^n n w^2_i)=\log n+\log\left\|{w}\right\|^{2}_{2}\leq\log n, $$

where we used the fact that $\left\|{w}\right\|_{2}^{2}\leq\left\|{w}\right\|_{1}=1$ for $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ . ∎

With these tools in hand, we turn to the proof of Thm. 4. For the runtime of LD, it follows from the fact that WeightedRPCholesky takes $O((d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}+r)nr)$ time and one step of AMD takes $O(nr)$ time.

The error analysis is different for the first adaptive iteration and the ensuing adaptive iterations. Roughly speaking, we will show that the first adaptive iteration brings the MMD gap to the desired level, while the ensuing iterations do not introduce an excessive amount of error.

Step 1. Bound $\Delta\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(w^{(1)})$

Let $K\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ and $F$ denote the low-rank approximation factor generated by WeightedRPCholesky. Denote $\widehat{K}\triangleq FF^{\top}$ . Then $K^{\prime}=\widehat{K}+\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K})$ . First, note that since $w^{(0)}=(\frac{1}{n},\ldots,\frac{1}{n})$ , Resample returns $\tilde{w}=w^{(0)}$ with probability one. By Lem. F.2, we have, using $\sqrt{a+b}\leq\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for $a,b\geq 0$ repeatedly and Lem. F.1 that $\tr((K-\widehat K)^w)\leq\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})$ and $\max_{i\in[n]}(K-\widehat{K})_{ii}\leq\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(1)}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{2\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})}+\sqrt{{w^{(1)}}^{\top}K^{\prime}w^{(1)}-w^{\prime\top}K^{\prime}w^{\prime}} \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{2\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})}+\sqrt{\frac{16\log n\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{T^{2}}}, $$

where we applied Lem. F.1 and Lem. F.3 in the last inequality. Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ . By Markov’s inequality, we have

$$ \textstyle\Pr(\sqrt{\lambda_1(K-\widehat K)} > \sqrt{\frac{\bE\left[\lambda_1(K - \widehat K)\right]}{\delta}})\leq\delta. $$

This means that with probability at least $1-\delta$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(1)}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{2\mathbb{E}\left[\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})\right]}{\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{16\log n\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{T^{2}}}. $$

Note that the lower bound condition on $r$ in Assum. ( α , β ) -params implies the lower bound condition in Prop. F.1. Hence, by Prop. F.1 with $w=(\frac{1}{n},\ldots,\frac{1}{n})$ and using the identity $\lambda_{1}(K-\widehat{K})\leq\tr(K-\widehat K)$ while noting that a factor of $n$ appears, we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(1)}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{2nH_{n,r}}{\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{16\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}\log n}{T^{2}}}. $$

Step 2. Bound the error of the remaining iterations

Fix $\delta>0$ . The previous step shows that, with probability at least $1-\frac{\delta}{2}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(1)}},\mathbb{P})\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{4nH_{n,r}}{\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{16\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}\log n}{T^{2}}}. $$

Fix $q>1$ , and let $\tilde{w}$ be the resampled weight defined in the $q$ -th iteration in Alg. 2. Without loss of generality, we assume $\tilde{w}_{i}>0$ for all $i>0$ , since if $w_{i}=0$ then index $i$ is irrelevant for the rest of the algorithm. Thus, thanks to Resample, we have $\tilde{w}_{i}\geq 1/n$ for all $i\in[n]$ . Let $a/b$ denote the entry-wise division between two vectors. As in the previous step of the proof, we let $K\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ , $F$ be the low-rank factor output by $\hyperref@@ii[alg:rpc]{\textup{WeightedRPCholesky}}({{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}},\mathcal{S}_{n},\tilde{w},r)$ , and $\widehat{K}=FF^{\top}$ . For any $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , recall the notation $K^{w}\triangleq\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w})K\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w})$ . Then we have

$$ \textstyle w^{\top}Kw \textstyle=(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}})^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(K^{\tilde{w}})(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}}) \textstyle=(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}})^{\top}(\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}})\widehat{K}\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}}))+\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}})(K-\widehat{K})\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}})))(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}}) \textstyle=w^{\top}\widehat{K}w+(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}})^{\top}(\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}})(K-\widehat{K})\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\tilde{w}})))(w/\sqrt{\tilde{w}}) \textstyle\leq w^{\top}\widehat{K}w+\max_{i\in[n]}(1/\tilde{w}_{i})\tr(\diag(\sqrt{\tilde w}) (K-\widehat K) \diag(\sqrt{\tilde w})) \textstyle\leq w^{\top}\widehat{K}w+n\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w} ). $$

Note that

$$ \textstyle K^{\prime}=\widehat{K}+\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K})=K+(\widehat{K}-K)+\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K}). $$

Since $K^{\prime}\succeq\widehat{K}$ , we have

$$ \textstyle{w^{(q)}}^{\top}\widehat{K}w^{(q)}\leq{w^{(q)}}^{\top}K^{\prime}w^{(q)}\leq\tilde{w}^{\top}K^{\prime}\tilde{w}, $$

where the last inequality follows from the if conditioning at the end of Alg. 2. In addition,

$$ \textstyle\tilde{w}^{\top}K^{\prime}\tilde{w} \textstyle=\tilde{w}^{\top}(K+(\widehat{K}-K)+\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K}))\tilde{w} \textstyle\leq\tilde{w}^{\top}K\tilde{w}+\tilde{w}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(K-\widehat{K})\tilde{w} \textstyle=\tilde{w}^{\top}K\tilde{w}+\sqrt{\tilde{w}}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}((K-\widehat{K})^{\tilde{w}})\sqrt{\tilde{w}} \textstyle\leq w^{\top}K\tilde{w}+\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w}), $$

where we used the fact that $K\succeq\widehat{K}$ and $\left\|{\sqrt{\tilde{w}}}\right\|_{2}=1$ . Plugging the previous inequality into (318) and then into (316) with $w=w^{(q)}$ , we get

$$ \textstyle{w^{(q)}}^{\top}Kw^{(q)} \textstyle\leq\tilde{w}^{\top}K\tilde{w}+(n+1)\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w}). $$

Taking square-root on both sides using $\sqrt{a+b}\leq\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for $a,b\geq 0$ and the triangle inequality, we get

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q)}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{\tilde{w}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{(n+1)\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w})} \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q-1)}},\mathbb{P})+\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q-1)}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{\tilde{w}})+\sqrt{(n+1)\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w})}. $$

By Markov’s inequality, we have

$$ \textstyle\Pr(\mmd_{\kp}(\bS_n^{w^{(q-1)}}, \bS_n^{\tilde w}) > \sqrt{\frac{4Q \bE\left[\mmd^2_{\kp}(\bS_n^{w^{(q-1)}}, \bS_n^{\tilde w})\right]}{\delta}}) \textstyle\leq\frac{\delta}{4Q} \textstyle\Pr(\sqrt{\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w})} > \sqrt{\frac{4Q\bE\left[\tr((K-\widehat K)^{\tilde w})\right]}{\delta}}) \textstyle\leq\frac{\delta}{4Q}. $$

By Prop. E.1(c), we have

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q-1)}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{\tilde{w}})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q-1)}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{\tilde{w}})\middle|w^{(q-1)}\right]\right]\leq\frac{\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{n}. $$

Thus by the union bound, with probability at least $1-\frac{\delta}{2Q}$ , using Prop. F.1 (recall low-rank approximation $\widehat{K}$ is obtained using $\tilde{w}$ ), we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q)}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{(q-1)}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{4Q\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{n\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{4Q(n+1)H_{n,r}}{\delta}}. $$

Finally, applying union bound and summing up the bounds for $q=1,\ldots,Q$ , we get, with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\Delta\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(w^{(q)})\leq\sqrt{\frac{2nH_{n,r}}{\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{16\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}\log n}{T^{2}}}+(Q-1)\left(\sqrt{\frac{4Q\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{n\delta}}+\sqrt{\frac{4Q(n+1)H_{n,r}}{\delta}}\right). $$

This matches the stated asymptotic bound in Thm. 4. ∎

### F.2 Thinning with KT-Compress++

For compression with target distribution $\mathbb{P}$ , we modify the original KT-Compress++ algorithm of [Shetty et al., 2022, Ex. 6]: in Halve and Thin of Compress++, we use kt-split with kernel ${{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ without kt-swap (so our version of Compress++ outputs $2^{\mathfrak{g}}$ coresets, each of size $\sqrt{n}$ ), followed by KT-Swap to obtain a size $\sqrt{n}$ coreset. We call the resulting thinning algorithm KT-Compress++. We show in Lems. F.4 and F.1 that KT-Compress++ satisfies an MMD guarantee similar to that of quadratic-time kernel thinning.

*Algorithm F.3 KT-Compress++ (modified Shetty et al. [2022, Alg. 2] to minimize MMD to $\mathbb{P}$ )*

```
Input: kernel ${{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ with zero-mean under $\mathbb{P}$ , input points $\mathcal{S}_{n}=(x_{i})_{i\in[n]}$ , multiplicity $n^{\prime}$ with $n^{\prime}\in 4^{\mathbb{N}}$ , weight $w\in\Delta_{n-1}\cap(\frac{\mathbb{N}_{0}}{n^{\prime}})^{n}$ , thinning parameter $\mathfrak{g}$ , failure probability $\delta$
$\mathtt{S}\leftarrow$ index sequence where $k\in[n]$ appears $n^{\prime}w_{k}$ times
$(\mathtt{I}^{(\ell)})_{\ell\in[2^{\mathfrak{g}}]}\leftarrow\textup{Compress++}(\mathfrak{g},\mathcal{S}_{n}[\mathtt{S}])$ $\triangleright$ Shetty et al. [2022, Ex. 6] with KT substituted with kt-split in Halve and Thin.
$\mathtt{I}^{(\ell)}\leftarrow\mathtt{S}[\mathtt{I}^{(\ell)}]$ for each $\ell\in[2^{\mathfrak{g}}]$
$\mathtt{I}\leftarrow\hyperref@@ii[alg:kt_swap_target]{\textup{KT-Swap}}({{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}},\mathcal{S}_{n},(\mathtt{I}^{(\ell)})_{\ell\in[2^{\mathfrak{g}}]})$
$w_{\textup{C++}}\leftarrow\text{simplex weights corresponding to }\mathtt{I}$ $\triangleright$ $w_{i}=\frac{\text{number of occurrences of }i\text{ in }\mathtt{I}}{\absolutevalue{\tI}}$
Return: $w_{\textup{C++}}\in\Delta_{n-1}\cap(\frac{\mathbb{N}_{0}}{\sqrt{n}})^{n}$ $\triangleright$ Hence $\left\|{w_{\textup{C++}}}\right\|_{0}\leq\sqrt{n}$
```

#### Lemma F.4 (Sub-gaussian guarantee for Compress++).

Let $\mathcal{S}_{n}$ be a sequence of $n$ points with $n\in 4^{\mathbb{N}}$ . For any $\delta\in(0,1)$ and integer $\mathfrak{g}\geq\lceil\log_{2}\log(n+1)+3.1\rceil$ , consider the Compress++ algorithm [Shetty et al., 2022, Algorithm 2] with thinning parameter $\mathfrak{g}$ , halving algorithm $\textsc{Halve}^{(k)}\triangleq\textup{symmetrized}(\textsc{kt-split}({\bm{k}},\cdot,1,\frac{n_{k}^{2}}{4n2^{\mathfrak{g}}(\mathfrak{g}+(\beta_{n}+1)2^{\mathfrak{g}})}\delta))$ 77 7 Any halving algorithm can be converted into an unbiased one by symmetrization, i.e., returning either the output half or its complement with equal probability [Shetty et al., 2022, Remark 3]. for an input of $n_{k}\triangleq 2^{\mathfrak{g}+1+k}\sqrt{n}$ points and $\beta_{n}\triangleq\log_{2}\left(\frac{n}{n_{0}}\right)$ , and with thinning algorithm $\textsc{Thin}\triangleq\textsc{kt-split}({\bm{k}},\cdot,\mathfrak{g},\frac{\mathfrak{g}}{\mathfrak{g}+(\beta_{n}+1)2^{\mathfrak{g}}}\delta)$ . Then this instantiation of Compress++ compresses $\mathcal{S}_{n}$ to $2^{\mathfrak{g}}$ coresets $(\mathcal{S}_{\textup{out}}^{(i)})_{i\in[2^{\mathfrak{g}}]}$ of $\sqrt{n}$ points each. Denote the signed measure $\phi^{(i)}\triangleq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{S}_{n}}\delta_{x}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{S}^{(i)}_{\textup{out}}}\delta_{x}$ . Then for each $i\in[2^{\mathfrak{g}}]$ , on an event $\mathcal{E}_{\textup{equi}}^{(i)}$ with $\Pr(\Eequi^{(i)})\geq 1-\frac{\delta}{2}$ , $\phi^{(i)}=\tilde{\phi}^{(i)}$ for a random signed measure $\tilde{\phi}^{(i)}$ such that, for any $\delta^{\prime}\in(0,1)$ ,

$$ \textstyle\Pr\left(\left\|{\tilde{\phi}^{(i)}{\bm{k}}}\right\|_{{\mathcal{H}_{{\bm{k}}}}}\geq a^{\prime}_{n}\left(1+\sqrt{\log(\frac{1}{\delta'})}\right)\right)\leq\delta^{\prime}, $$

where

$$ \textstyle a^{\prime}_{n}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{n}}\left(2+\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}\|{{\bm{k}}}\|_{n}\log(\frac{6\sqrt{n}(\fg+ (\frac{\log_2 n}{2} - \fg)2^\fg)}{\delta})\log(4\cvrnum{\k}\left(\balleuc(R_{n}), n^{-1/2}\right))}\right). $$

#### Proof of Lem. F.4.

By Lem. D.1, with notation $t\triangleq\log\frac{1}{\delta^{\prime}}$ , there exist events $\mathcal{E}_{k,j}$ , $\mathcal{E}_{\textup{T}}$ , and random signed measures $\phi_{k,j}$ , $\tilde{\phi}_{k,j}$ , $\phi_{\textup{T}}$ , $\tilde{\phi}_{\textup{T}}$ for $0\leq k\leq\beta_{n}$ and $j\in[4^{k}]$ such that

#### Corollary F.1 (MMD guarantee for Compress++).

Let $\mathcal{S}_{\infty}$ be an infinite sequence of points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and ${\bm{k}}$ a kernel. For any $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $n\in 4^{\mathbb{N}}$ , consider the Compress++ with the same parameters as in Lem. F.4 with $\mathfrak{g}\geq\lceil\log_{2}\log(n+1)+3.1\rceil$ . Then for any $i\in[\sqrt{n}]$ , with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n},\mathbb{S}^{(i)}_{\textup{out}})\leq\frac{4}{\sqrt{n}}\left(2+\sqrt{\frac{8}{3}\|{{\bm{k}}}\|_{n}\log(\frac{6\sqrt{n}(\fg+ (\frac{\log_2 n}{2} - \fg)2^\fg)}{\delta})\log(4\cvrnum{\k}\left(\balleuc(R_{n}), n^{-1/2}\right))}\right)\left(1+\sqrt{\log\frac{2}{\delta}}\right). $$

#### Proof.

After applying Lem. F.4 with $\delta^{\prime}=\frac{\delta}{2}$ and following the same argument as in the proof of Cor. D.1, we have, with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{\bm{k}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n},\mathbb{S}^{(i)}_{\textup{out}})\leq a_{n}^{\prime}\left(1+\sqrt{\log\frac{2}{\delta}}\right). $$

Plugging in the expression of $a_{n}^{\prime}$ from Lem. F.4 gives the claimed bound. ∎

### F.3 Proof of Thm. 5: Theorem 5 (MMD guarantee for LSKT).

First of all, the claimed runtime follows from the runtime of LD (Thm. 4), the $O(d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}4^{\mathfrak{g}}n\log n)$ runtime of Compress++, and the $O(d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}n^{1.5})$ runtime of KT-Swap.

Without loss of generality assume $n\in 4^{\mathbb{N}}$ . Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ . Let $w^{\diamond}$ denote the output of LD, and $w^{\textup{sr}}$ denote the output of Resample, both regarded as random variables. By Thm. 4, we have, with probability at least $1-\frac{\delta}{3}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P})=\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{{w_{\textsc{OPT}}}},\mathbb{P})+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{nH_{n,r}}{\delta}}\right)+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}\max(\log n,1/\delta)}{n}}\right). $$

By Prop. E.1(c) with ${\bm{k}}={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ , we have the upper bound

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{sr}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{{\diamond}}})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{sr}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{{\diamond}}})\middle|w^{\diamond}\right]\right]\leq\frac{\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{n}. $$

Thus, by Markov’s inequality,

$$ \textstyle\Pr(\mmd_{\kp}(\bS_n^{w^\truncstrat}, \bS_n^{w^{\db}}) \ge\sqrt{\frac{3\kpnormSn}{n\delta}})\leq\frac{\delta}{3}. $$

Hence, with probability at least $1-\frac{\delta}{3}$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\textup{sr}}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{{\diamond}}})\leq\sqrt{\frac{3\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}}{n\delta}}. $$

Let $\mathbb{S}_{\textup{out}}^{(i)}$ denote the $i$ -th coreset output by Thin in KT-Compress++ (Alg. F.3). By Cor. F.1 with ${\bm{k}}={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ , we have, with probability at least $1-\frac{\delta}{3}$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}^{w^{\textup{sr}}}_{n},\mathbb{S}^{(i)}_{\textup{out}})=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n}\log n\log(e\cvrnum{\kp}(\balleuc(R_{n}), n^{-1/2})))}{n}}\log\frac{e}{\delta}\right). $$

Since KT-Swap can never increase $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\cdot,\mathbb{P})$ , we have, by the triangle inequality,

By the union bound, with probability at least $1-\delta$ , the bounds (342), (345), (347) hold, so that the claim is shown by adding together the right-hand sides of these bounds and applying Assum. ( α , β )-kernel. ∎

In this section, we provide deferred analyses for RT and SR/LSR, as well as the algorithmic details of Recombination (Alg. G.1) and KT-Swap-LS (Alg. G.2).

*Algorithm G.1 Recombination (rephrasing of Tchernychova [2016, Alg. 1] that takes $O(nm+m^{3}\log n)$ time)*

```
Input: matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ with $m<n$ and one row of $A$ all positive, a nonnegative vector $x_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}$ .
function FindBFS( $A,x_{0}$ )
$\triangleright$ The requirement of $A$ and $x_{0}$ are the same as the input. This subroutine takes $O(n^{3})$ time.
$x\leftarrow x_{0}$
$U,S,V^{\top}\leftarrow\textrm{SVD}(A)$ $\triangleright$ any $O(n^{3})$ -time SVD algorithm that gives $USV^{\top}=A$
$V\leftarrow(V^{\top})_{m+1:n}$ $\triangleright$ $V\in\mathbb{R}^{(n-m)\times n}$ so that the null space of $A$ is spanned by the rows of $V$
for $i=1$ to $n-m$ do
$v\leftarrow V_{i}$
$k\leftarrow\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{j\in[n]:v_{j}>0}\frac{x_{j}}{v_{j}}$ $\triangleright$ This must succeed because $Av=0$ and $A$ has an all-positive row, so one of the coordinates of $v$ must be positive.
$x\leftarrow x-\frac{x_{k}}{v_{k}}v$ $\triangleright$ This zeros out the $k$ -th coordinate of $x$ while still ensuring $x$ is nonnegative.
for $j=i+1$ to $n-m$ do
$V_{j}\leftarrow V_{j}-\frac{V_{j,k}}{v_{k}}v$ $\triangleright$ $\{V_{j}\}_{j={i+1}}^{n-m}$ remain independent and have $0$ on the $k$ -th coordinate.
end for
end for
return: $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}$ such that $Ax=Ax_{0}$ and $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}\leq m$ .
end function
$x\leftarrow x_{0}$
while $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}>2m$ do
Divide $\{i\in[n]:x_{i}>0\}$ into $2m$ index blocks $\mathtt{I}_{1},\ldots,\mathtt{I}_{2m}$ , each of size at most $\left\lfloor\frac{\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}}{2m}\right\rfloor$ .
$A_{i}\leftarrow A_{:,\mathtt{I}_{i}}x_{\mathtt{I}_{i}}\in\mathbb{R}^{m},\forall i\in[2m]$ $\triangleright$ Since $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}$ is halved in each iteration, overall this step takes $O(nm)$ time.
Form $\hat{A}$ to be the $m\times 2m$ matrix with columns $A_{i}$ $\triangleright$ Hence, one row of $A$ contains all positive entries.
$\hat{x}\leftarrow\textrm{FindFBS}(\hat{A},\bm{1}_{2m})$ $\triangleright$ $\left\|{\hat{x}}\right\|_{0}\leq n$ and $\hat{A}\hat{x}=\sum A_{i}\hat{x}_{i}=\sum A_{i}=\sum A_{:,\mathtt{I}_{i}}x_{\mathtt{I}_{i}}=Ax$ .
for $i=1$ to $2m$ do
$x_{\mathtt{I}_{i}}\leftarrow\hat{x}_{i}\cdot x_{\mathtt{I}_{i}}$ if $\hat{x}_{i}>0$ else $0$
end for
$\triangleright$ After the update, $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}$ is halved while the equality $Ax=Ax_{0}$ is maintained.
end while
if $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}\geq m+1$ then
$\mathtt{I}\leftarrow\{i\in[n]:x_{i}>0\}$
$x_{\mathtt{I}}=\textrm{FindBFS}(A_{:,\mathtt{I}},x_{\mathtt{I}})$
end if
Return: $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}_{\geq 0}$ such that $Ax=Ax_{0}$ and $\left\|{x}\right\|_{0}\leq m$ .
```

*Algorithm G.2 KT-Swap with Linear Search (KT-Swap-LS)*

```
Input: kernel ${{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}$ with zero-mean under $\mathbb{P}$ , input points $\mathcal{S}_{n}=(x_{i})_{i\in[n]}$ , weights $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ , $\texttt{fmt}\in\{\textup{SPLX},\textup{CP}\}$
$\mathtt{S}\leftarrow\{i\in[n]:w_{i}\neq 0\}$
$\triangleright$ Maintain two sufficient statistics: $g=Kw$ and $D=w^{\top}Kw$ .
function Add( $g,D,i,t$ )
$g\leftarrow g+t{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},x_{i})$
$D\leftarrow D+2tg_{i}+t^{2}{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(x_{i},x_{i})$
return: $(g,D)$
end function
function Scale( $g,D,\alpha$ )
$g\leftarrow\alpha g$
$D\leftarrow\alpha^{2}D$
return: $(g,D)$
end function
$\texttt{Kdiag}\leftarrow{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$
$g\leftarrow\bm{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$
$D\leftarrow 0$
for $i$ in $\mathtt{S}$ do
$(g,D)\leftarrow\textrm{Add}(g,D,i,w_{i})$
end for
for $i$ in $\mathtt{S}$ do
if $w_{i}=1$ then continue; $\triangleright$ We cannot swap $i$ out if $\sum_{j\neq i}w_{j}=0$ !
$\triangleright$ First zero out $w_{i}$ .
$(g,D)\leftarrow\textrm{Add}(g,D,i,-w_{i})$
$(g,D)\leftarrow\textrm{Scale}(g,D,\frac{1}{1-w_{i}})$
$w_{i}=0$
$\triangleright$ Next perform line search to add back a point.
$\alpha=(D-g)./(D-2g+\texttt{Kdiag})$ ; $\triangleright$ $\alpha_{i}=\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{t}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{te_{i}+(1-t)w},\mathbb{P})=\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{t}(1-t)^{2}D+2t(1-t)g+t^{2}\texttt{Kdiag}$
if $\texttt{fmt}=\textup{SPLX}$ then
$\alpha=\texttt{clip}(\alpha,0,1)$ ; $\triangleright$ Clipping $\alpha$ to $[0,1]$ . This corresponds to $\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{t\in[0,1]}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{te_{i}+(1-t)w},\mathbb{P})$ .
end if
$D^{\prime}\leftarrow(1-\alpha)^{2}D+2\alpha(1-\alpha)g+\alpha^{2}\texttt{Kdiag}$ $\triangleright$ multiplications are element-wise
$k\leftarrow\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{i}D^{\prime}_{i}$
$(g,D)\leftarrow\textrm{Scale}(g,D,1-\alpha_{k})$
$(g,D)\leftarrow\textrm{Add}(g,D,k,\alpha_{k})$
end for
Return: $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$
```

### G.1 MMD guarantee for RT

We start by stating the MMD guarantee of RT, a result that might be of independent interest.

#### Proposition G.1 (RT guarantee).

Under Assums. 1 and ( α , β )-kernel, given $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ and that $m\geq(\frac{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}+1}{\sqrt{\log 2}}+\sqrt{\log 2})^{2}-\frac{1}{\log 2}+1$ , RecombinationThinning (Alg. 4) outputs $w_{{\textup{RT}}}\in\Delta_{n-1}$ with $\left\|{w_{{\textup{RT}}}}\right\|_{0}\leq m$ in $O((d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}+m)nm+m^{3}\log n)$ time such that with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

where $H_{n,r}$ is defined in (290).

#### Proof of Prop. G.1.

The runtime follows from the $O((d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}+m)nm)$ runtime of WeightedRPCholesky, the $O(d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}nm)$ runtime of KT-Swap-LS, and the $O(nm+m^{3}\log n)$ runtime of Recombination [Tchernychova, 2016] which dominates the $O(m^{3})$ weight optimization step.

Recall $w^{\prime}\in\Delta_{n-1}$ from RT. The formation of $F$ in Alg. 4 is identical to the formation of $F$ (with $r=m-1$ ) in Alg. 2 for $q>1$ . Thus by (316) with $w=w^{\prime}$ , $K={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ ,

$$ \textstyle{w^{\prime}}^{\top}Kw^{\prime}\leq{w^{\prime}}^{\top}FF^{\top}w^{\prime}+n\tr((K - FF^\top)^{\tilde w}), $$

where $K={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ . By construction of $w^{\prime}$ using Recombination, we have $F^{\top}\tilde{w}=F^{\top}w^{\prime}$ . Since $K\succeq FF^{\top}$ , we have

We recognize the right-hand side is precisely the right-hand side of (323) aside from having a multiplier of $n$ instead of $n+1$ in front of the trace and that $F$ is rank $m-1$ . In this section, we provide deferred analyses for CT and SC/LSC.

### H.1 MMD guarantee for CT

#### Proposition H.1 (CT guarantee).

Under Assums. 1 and ( α , β )-kernel, given $w\in\Delta_{n-1}$ and $m\geq(\frac{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}+1}{\sqrt{\log 2}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{\log 2}})^{2}-\frac{1}{\log 2}$ , CT outputs $w_{{\textup{CT}}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $\bm{1}_{n}^{\top}w_{{\textup{CT}}}=1$ and $\left\|{w_{{\textup{CT}}}}\right\|_{0}\leq m$ in $O((d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}+m)nm+m^{3})$ time such that, for any $\delta\in(0,1)$ , with probability $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w_{{\textup{CT}}}},\mathbb{P})\leq 2\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{4H_{n,m^{\prime}}}{\delta}}, $$

where $H_{n,m}$ is defined in (290) and $m^{\prime}\triangleq m+\log 2-2\sqrt{m\log 2+1}$ .

#### Proof of Prop. H.1.

The runtime follows from the $O((d_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}+m)nm)$ runtime of WeightedRPCholesky, the $O(nm)$ runtime of KT-Swap-LS, and the $O(m^{3})$ runtime of matrix inversion in solving the two minimization problems using (375).

To improve the clarity of notation, we will use $w^{\diamond}$ to denote the input weight $w$ to CT. For index sequences $\mathtt{I},\mathtt{J}\subset[n]$ and a kernel ${\bm{k}}$ , we use ${\bm{k}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{J})$ to indicate the matrix ${\bm{k}}(\mathcal{S}_{n}[\mathtt{I}],\mathcal{S}_{n}[\mathtt{J}])=[{\bm{k}}(x_{i},x_{j})]_{i\in\mathtt{I},j\in\mathtt{J}}$ , and similarly for a function $f:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}$ , we use $f(\mathtt{I})$ to denote the vector $(f(x_{i}))_{i\in\mathtt{I}}$ .

Recall the regularized kernel is ${{\bm{k}}_{c}}\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}+c$ . Suppose for now that $c>0$ is an arbitrary constant. Let $\mathtt{I}$ denote the indices output by WeightedRPCholesky in CT. Let

$$ \textstyle w^{c}\triangleq\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w:\supp(w)\subset\mathtt{I}}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}). $$

Note that $w^{c}$ is not a probability vector and may not sum to $1$ .

Step 1. Bound $\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}})$ in terms of WeightedRPCholesky approximation error

We start by using an argument similar to that of Epperly and Moreno [2024, Prop. 3] to exploit the optimality condition of $w^{c}$ . Since

$$ \textstyle\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w:\supp(w)\subset\mathtt{I}}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}) \textstyle=\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w:\supp(w)\subset\mathtt{I}}w_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})w_{\mathtt{I}}-2{w^{{\diamond}}}^{\top}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathtt{I})w_{\mathtt{I}}, $$

by optimality, $w^{c}$ satisfies,

$$ \textstyle{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})w^{c}_{\mathtt{I}}=\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I}). $$

We comment that the index sequence $\mathtt{I}$ returned by WeightedRPCholesky makes ${{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})$ invertible with probability $1$ : by the Guttman rank additivity formula of Schur complement [Zhang, 2006, Eq. (6.0.4)], each iteration of WeightedRPCholesky chooses a pivot with a non-zero diagonal and thus increases the rank of the low-rank approximation matrix, which is spanned by the columns of pivots, by $1$ . Hence

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\cdot) \textstyle={{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\cdot,\mathcal{S}_{n})w^{c}={{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\cdot,\mathtt{I})w^{c}_{\mathtt{I}}={{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\cdot,\mathtt{I}){{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})^{-1}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})w^{c}_{\mathtt{I}} \textstyle={{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\cdot,\mathtt{I}){{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})^{-1}\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I})=\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}}(\cdot), $$

where ${{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}}(x,y)\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(x,\mathtt{I}){{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})^{-1}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathtt{I},y)$ . Then

$$ \textstyle\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}) \textstyle=\left\|{\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}-\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}\right\|^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}=\left\|{\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}-\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}{{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}}}\right\|^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}={w^{\diamond}}^{\top}({{\bm{k}}_{c}}-{{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}})(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})w^{\diamond}. $$

Recall the index set $\mathtt{I}$ consists of the $m$ pivots selected by WeightedRPCholesky on the input matrix

$$ \textstyle K^{\diamond}_{c}\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{c}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})^{w^{\diamond}}. $$

Define

$$ \textstyle\widehat{K}^{\diamond}_{c}\triangleq{{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})^{w^{\diamond}}. $$

Thus, by Lem. F.1,

$$ \textstyle\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}}) \textstyle={w^{\diamond}}^{\top}({{\bm{k}}_{c}}-{{\bm{k}}_{c}}_{\mathtt{I}})(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})w^{\diamond}=\sqrt{w^{\diamond}}^{\top}(K^{\diamond}_{c}-\widehat{K}^{\diamond}_{c})\sqrt{w^{\diamond}}\leq\lambda_{1}(K^{\diamond}_{c}-\widehat{K}^{\diamond}_{c})\leq\tr(K^\db_c - \widehat K^\db_c). $$

Step 2. Bound $\tr(K^\db_c - \widehat K^\db_c)$ using the trace bound of the unregularized kernel

Let ${\llbracket{A}\rrbracket}_{r}$ denote the best rank- $r$ approximation of an SPSD matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ in the sense that

$$ \textstyle{\llbracket{A}\rrbracket}_{r} \textstyle\triangleq\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{\begin{subarray}{c}X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\\
X=X^{\top}\\
A\succeq X\succeq 0\\
\rank(X)\leq r\end{subarray}}\tr(A - X). $$

By the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem applied to symmetric matrices [Dax, 2014, Theorem 19], the solution to (361) is given by $r$ -truncated eigenvalue decomposition of $A$ , so that

$$ \textstyle\tr(A - \bestapprox{A}_r)=\sum_{\ell=r+1}^{n}\lambda_{\ell}(A). $$

Let $q\triangleq\mathfrak{U}(m)$ where $\mathfrak{U}$ is defined in (291), so that by Chen et al. [2022, Thm. 3.1] with $\epsilon=1$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\tr(K_c^\db- \widehat{K}_c^\db)\right]\leq 2\tr(K_c^\db- \bestapprox{K_c^\db}_{q}). $$

We know one specific rank- $q$ approximation of $K_{c}^{\diamond}$ :

$$ \textstyle\widetilde{K}_{c}^{\diamond}\triangleq{\llbracket{K^{\diamond}}\rrbracket}_{q-1}+\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w^{\diamond}})c\bm{1}_{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w^{\diamond}}), $$

which satisfies

$$ \textstyle K^{\diamond}_{c}-\widetilde{K}_{c}^{\diamond} \textstyle=K^{\diamond}+\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w^{\diamond}})c\bm{1}_{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w^{\diamond}})-\widetilde{K}_{c}^{\diamond}=K^{\diamond}-{\llbracket{K^{\diamond}}\rrbracket}_{q-1}. $$

Thus by the variational definition in (361), we have

$$ \textstyle\tr(K^\db_c - \bestapprox{K^\db_c}_{q})\leq\tr(K^\db_c - \widetilde K^\db_c)=\tr(K^\db- \bestapprox{K^\db}_{q-1})=\sum_{\ell=q}^{n}\lambda_{\ell}(K^{\diamond}). $$

Note the last bound does not depend on $c$ . The tail sum of eigenvalues in the last expression is the same (up to a constant multiplier) as the one in (292) except for an off-by-1 difference in the summation index. A simple calculation shows that for $m^{\prime}\triangleq m+\log 2-2\sqrt{m\log 2+1}$ , we have $\mathfrak{U}(m^{\prime})=\mathfrak{U}(m)-1$ . Another simple calculation shows that $m\geq(\frac{\mathfrak{C}_{d}R_{n}^{\beta}+1}{\sqrt{\log 2}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{\log 2}})^{2}-\frac{1}{\log 2}$ implies that $m^{\prime}$ satisfies the lower bound requirement of $r$ in Prop. F.1. Thus, arguing as in the proof that follows (292), we get

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}\left[\tr(K_c^\db- \widehat K_c^{\db})\right]\leq H_{n,m^{\prime}}. $$

Thus so far we have shown

$$ \textstyle\mathbb{E}[\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}})]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\tr(K_c^\db- \widehat{K}_c^\db)\right]\leq H_{n,m^{\prime}}. $$

By Markov’s inequality, with probability at least $1-\delta$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}})\leq\sqrt{\frac{H_{n,m^{\prime}}}{\delta}}. $$

Recall that $\mmd_{{\bm{k}}}(\mu,\nu)=\left\|{(\mu-\nu){\bm{k}}}\right\|_{{\bm{k}}}$ for signed measures $\mu,\nu$ . By the triangle inequality, we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}})+\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle=\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}})+\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P}), $$

where we used that fact that $\sum_{i\in[n]}w^{\diamond}_{i}=1$ to get the identity $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P})=\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P})$ . Hence, with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{P})\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P})+\sqrt{\frac{H_{n,m^{\prime}}}{\delta}}. $$

Step 3. Incorporating sum-to-one constraint

We now turn $w^{c}$ into a constant-preserving weight while not inflating the MMD by much. Define

$$ \textstyle w^{1}\triangleq\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w:\supp(w)\subset\mathtt{I},\sum_{i\in[n]}w_{i}=1}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{P}). $$

Note $w^{1}$ is the weight right before KT-Swap-LS step in CT. Let $K_{\mathtt{I}}={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathtt{I},\mathtt{I})$ . Let $\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}$ denote the $\absolutevalue{\tI}$ -dimensional all-one veector. The Karush-Kuhm-Tucker condition [Ghojogh et al., 2021, Sec. 4.7] applied to (373) implies that, the solution $w^{1}$ is a stationary point of the Lagrangian function

$$ \textstyle L(w_{\mathtt{I}},\lambda)\triangleq w_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}w_{\mathtt{I}}+\lambda(\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}w_{\mathtt{I}}-1). $$

Then $\nabla_{w_{\mathtt{I}}}L(w_{\mathtt{I}}^{1},\lambda)=0$ implies $2K_{\mathtt{I}}w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}-\lambda\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=0$ , so $w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=\frac{\lambda K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{2}$ . The Lagrangian multiplier $\lambda$ is determined by the constraint $\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}w_{\mathtt{I}}=1$ , so we find

$$ \textstyle w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=\frac{K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}. $$

Define

$$ \textstyle w^{c,\mathbb{P}}\triangleq\mathop{\mathrm{}}{argmin}_{w:\supp(w)\subset\mathtt{I}}\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w},\mathbb{P}). $$

Since $w^{c,\mathbb{P}}$ is optimized to minimize $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}$ to $\mathbb{P}$ on the same support as $w^{c}$ , we have

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{P}). $$

The optimality condition for $w^{c,\mathbb{P}}$ is

$$ \textstyle(K_{\mathtt{I}}+c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top})w-c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=0, $$

and hence by the Sherman–Morrison formula,

$$ \textstyle w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}=(K_{\mathtt{I}}+c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top})^{-1}c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=\left(K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}-\frac{cK^{-1}_{\mathtt{I}}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}}{1+c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}\right)c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=\frac{K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{1/c+\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}. $$

Let $\rho_{c}\triangleq\frac{\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{1/c+\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}$ , so that $w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}=\rho_{c}w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}$ . In particular, $w^{1}$ and $w^{c,\mathbb{P}}$ are scalar multiples of one another. To relate $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{1}},\mathbb{P})$ and $\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})$ , note that

$$ \textstyle\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{1}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle={w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}w^{1}_{\mathtt{I}}=\frac{{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}}{\rho^{2}_{c}}=\frac{{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}}^{\top}(K_{\mathtt{I}}+c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top})w^{c,\mathbb{P}}_{\mathtt{I}}-c(\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}w_{\mathtt{I}}^{c})^{2}}{\rho^{2}_{c}} \textstyle=\frac{\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})+2c\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}w_{\mathtt{I}}^{c}-c-c(\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}w_{\mathtt{I}}^{c})^{2}}{\rho^{2}_{c}}=\frac{\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})-c(\rho_{c}-1)^{2}}{\rho^{2}_{c}}. $$

So far the argument does not depend on any particular choice of $c>0$ . Let us now discuss how to choose $c$ . Note that

$$ \textstyle\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}} \textstyle=m\frac{\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{\sqrt{m}}^{\top}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\frac{\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}{\sqrt{m}}\geq m\lambda_{m}(K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1})\geq\frac{m}{\lambda_{1}(K_{\mathtt{I}})}\geq\frac{m}{\tr(K_\tI)}\geq\frac{m}{\sum_{i\in[m]}\operatorname{diag}(K)^{\downarrow}_{i}}, $$

where $\operatorname{diag}(K)^{\downarrow}$ denote the diagonal entries of $K={{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(\mathcal{S}_{n},\mathcal{S}_{n})$ sorted in descending order. Thus

$$ \textstyle\rho_{c} \textstyle=\frac{1}{\frac{1}{c\bm{1}^{\top}_{\mathtt{I}}K_{\mathtt{I}}^{-1}\bm{1}_{\mathtt{I}}}+1}\geq\frac{1}{\frac{\sum_{i\in[m]}\operatorname{diag}(K)^{\downarrow}_{i}}{mc}+1}. $$

Hence we can choose $c$ to make sure $\rho_{c}$ is bounded from below by a positive value. Recall in CT, we take

$$ \textstyle c=\frac{\sum_{i\in[m]}\operatorname{diag}(K)^{\downarrow}_{i}}{m}, $$

so that $\rho_{c}\geq\frac{1}{2}$ and

$$ \textstyle\mmd^{2}_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{1}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle=\frac{\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})-c(\rho_{c}-1)^{2}}{\rho^{2}_{c}}\leq 4\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}^{2}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P}). $$

Hence by (372) and the fact that KT-Swap-LS and the final reweighting in CT only improves MMD, we have, with probability at least $1-\delta$ ,

$$ \textstyle\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w_{{\textup{CT}}}},\mathbb{P})\leq\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{1}},\mathbb{P}) \textstyle\leq 2\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c,\mathbb{P}}},\mathbb{P})\leq 2\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{c}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{c}},\mathbb{P})\leq 2\mmd_{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}(\mathbb{S}_{n}^{w^{\diamond}},\mathbb{P})+2\sqrt{\frac{H_{n,m^{\prime}}}{\delta}}, $$

where we use 372 in the last inequality. ∎

The claimed runtime follows from the runtime of SteinThinning (Alg. D.1) or LD (Thm. 4) plus the runtime of CT (Prop. H.1).

## Appendix I Implementation and Experimental Details

In this section, we collect experimental details that were deferred from Sec. 5.

### I.1 $O(d)$ -time Stein kernel evaluation

In this section, we show that for $\mathcal{S}_{n}=(x_{i})_{i\in[n]}$ , each Stein kernel evaluation ${{\bm{k}}_{p}}(x_{i},x_{j})$ for a radially analytic base kernel (Def. B.3) can be done in $O(d)$ time after computing certain sufficient statistics in $O(nd^{2}+d^{3})$ time. Let $M\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ be a positive definite preconditioning matrix for ${{\bm{k}}_{p}}$ . Let $L$ be the Cholesky decomposition of $M$ which can be done in $O(d^{3})$ time so that $M=LL^{\top}$ . From the expression (B.5), we can achieve $O(d)$ time evaluation if we can compute $\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{M}^{2}$ and $M\nabla\log p(x)$ in $O(d)$ time. For $M\nabla\log p(x)$ , we can simply precompute $M\nabla\log p(x_{i})$ for all $i\in[n]$ . For $\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{M}^{2}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\left\|{x-y}\right\|_{M}^{2}=(x-y)^{\top}M^{-1}(x-y)=(x-y)^{\top}(LL^{\top})^{-1}(x-y)=\left\|{L^{-1}(x-y)}\right\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Hence it suffices to precompute $L^{-1}x_{i}$ for all $i\in[n]$ , and we can precompute the inverse $L^{-1}$ in $O(d^{3})$ time.

### I.2 Default parameters for algorithms

For LD, we always use $Q=3$ . To ensure that the guarantees of Lems. F.3 and 4 hold while achieving fast convergence in practice, we take the step size of AMD to be $1/(8\|{{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}}\|_{n})$ in the first adaptive round and $1/(8\sum_{i\in[n]}w_{i}^{(q-1)}{{\bm{k}}_{\mathbb{P}}}(x_{i},x_{i}))$ in subsequent adaptive rounds. We use $T=7\sqrt{n_{0}}$ for AMD in all experiments.

We implemented our modified versions of KernelThinning and KT-Compress++ in JAX [Bradbury et al., 2018] so that certain subroutines can achieve a speedup using just-in-time compilation and the parallel computation power of GPUs. For Compress++, we use $\mathfrak{g}=4$ in all experiments as in Shetty et al. [2022]. For both KernelThinning and KT-Compress++, we use choose $\delta=1/2$ as in the goodpoints library.

Each experiment was run with a single NVIDIA RTX 6000 GPU and an AMD EPYC 7513 32-Core CPU.

### I.4 Correcting for approximate MCMC details

Surrogate ground truth Following Liu and Lee [2017], we took the first 10,000 data points and generated $2^{20}$ surrogate ground truth sample points using NUTS [Hoffman and Gelman, 2014] for the evaluation. To generate the surrogate ground truth using NUTS, we used numpyro [Phan et al., 2019]. It took $12$ hours to generate the surrogate ground truth points using the GPU implementation, and we estimate it would have taken $200$ hours using the CPU implementation.

SGFS For SGFS, we used batch size 32 and the step size schedule $\eta/(1+t)^{0.55}$ where $t$ is the step count and $\eta$ is the initial step size. We chose $\eta$ from $\{10.0,5.0,1.0,0.5,0.1,0.05,0.01\}$ , found $\eta=1.0$ gave the best standard thinning MMD to get a coreset size of $m=2^{10}$ , and hence we fixed $\eta=1.0$ in all experiments. We used the version of SGFS [Ahn et al., 2012, SGFS-f] that involves inversion of $d\times d$ matrices — we found the faster version (SGFS-d) that inverts only the diagonal resulted in significantly worse mixing. We implemented SGFS in numpy and ran it on the CPU.

Runtime The SGFS chain of length $2^{24}$ took approximately 2 hours to generate using the CPU. Remarkably, all of our low-rank methods finish within 10 minutes for $n_{0}=2^{20}$ , which is orders of magnitude faster than the time taken to generate the NUTS surrogate ground truth.
